Both sides openly discussed past differences and agreed to deepen cooperation on trade, energy, transport, and people-to-people ties, with bilateral trade reaching about $600 million in nine months, up from $401 million in 2025.



The reset supports Azerbaijan’s push to diversify partnerships toward Asia, but its durability depends on managing India’s arms sales to Armenia and Azerbaijan’s bid to join the Shanghai Cooperation Organization as a full member.
